column1: # Native PathMap prefix restriction frontier: focused zipper graft versus bulk restrict.
# Experiment checkpoint: 87f367b83. Selected production checkpoint: c460eb922.
# Host: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5975WX, 32 physical cores, SMT disabled; CPU 8 pinned.
# Preflight: 81.87% aggregate idle; CPU 8 was 97.99% idle; 52 GiB available memory; zero swap used.
# Command: systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 taskset -c 8 cargo bench -j 4 -p models --bench epathmap_restrict_frontier --features epathmap-restrict-differential
# Design: 60 retained paired/interleaved samples after 10 warmups per cell; arm order rotated each repetition; exactly one run.

# Fixture: 4,096 source values; singleton prefix, 64 disjoint prefixes with 64B/4096B values, nested overlap, empty/root/no-hit masks, 128-byte deep shared prefixes, and root fallback plus exact prefixes.
# Correctness: exact keys, associated Par values, and ACTree03 topology asserted before timing, including value-free endpoints.
# Result: ACCEPTED by pgmcp experiment/hypothesis 254. Welch t=-17.4911770425, p=5.5465680365e-55, Cohen's d=-1.0644791359, 95% CI [-6952.2935,-5548.4103] ns.
# Robustness: Cliff's delta=-0.504976; Mann-Whitney p=0.0. The nonparametric result agrees.

# Decision: exactly one value-bearing selector uses a focused zipper graft; every other cardinality uses native PathMap::restrict. This is a semantic cardinality dispatch, not an empirical size cutoff.
# Resources: 24,808 KiB peak RSS; 8,192 MiB MemoryMax; zero swap.
